---
description: 'Accessibility guidance for the dashboard'
applyTo: 'dashboard/*.html,dashboard/*.css,dashboard/*.js'
---

# Dashboard accessibility

- Use semantic HTML and a logical heading order. Give each page a title and declare its language.
- Use native controls where possible; label form fields and give icon-only controls accessible names.
- Make interactive features usable with a keyboard, preserve visible focus, and keep focus order logical.
- Ensure text and controls have sufficient contrast. Do not rely on color alone to communicate state.
- Support zoom and narrow screens without losing content or functionality. Respect reduced-motion preferences when adding animation.
- Provide meaningful alternative text for informative images; mark decorative images appropriately.
- Check changed interactions with keyboard navigation and, when practical, a screen reader.
